title: 2D dungeon layout algorithms: room placement, Delaunay, MST
description: Pure-Java algorithm classes for the first three stages of the vazgriz dungeon pipeline (https://vazgriz.com/119/procedurally-generated-dungeons/). These live in ixdar.procgen.dungeon.algo and have no MeshNode dependency so they can be unit-tested in isolation. RoomPlacer: deterministic seeded random AABB placement in an integer grid with a 1-unit buffer between rooms to prevent adjacency. Retries placement on collision up to a configurable attempt cap. Mirror RandomValueNode's seed handling pattern. DelaunayTriangulation2D: Bowyer-Watson algorithm over room centers. Returns an EdgeGraphValue whose nodes are room indices. PrimMinimumSpanningTree: Prim's algorithm over the Delaunay edges (weighted by Euclidean distance between room centers), plus a pass that adds each non-MST Delaunay edge with probability extraEdgeProb (default 0.125 per vazgriz) using a separate seeded RNG stream so the extra-edge pass is reproducible independently of placement. All three must be fully deterministic: same seed + same inputs -> same outputs, byte-for-byte.
definition-of-done: 1. RoomPlacer.place(seed, gridW, gridH, roomCount, minSize, maxSize, maxAttempts) returns RoomListValue. 2. DelaunayTriangulation2D.triangulate(rooms) returns EdgeGraphValue covering the convex hull of room centers. 3. PrimMinimumSpanningTree.build(edges, roomCenters, extraEdgeProb, seed) returns EdgeGraphValue that (a) spans all rooms, (b) is a subset of the input edges plus probabilistic extras. 4. No use of System.currentTimeMillis or Math.random — all randomness comes from the seed input. 5. Public API is narrow (one static method per class); internal helpers are package-private.
testing-plan: 1. Determinism: same seed -> identical RoomListValue (byte-compare serialized form). 2. Room non-overlap: no two placed rooms' AABBs intersect, 1-unit buffer respected. 3. Delaunay correctness: every triangle's circumscribed circle contains no other room center (the empty-circle property). 4. MST spans: output graph is connected, has exactly N-1 edges if extraEdgeProb=0. 5. MST optimality: total edge weight equals known-good MST for a hand-constructed 5-room test case. 6. Extra-edge determinism: same seed + same MST -> same set of extra edges across runs.
todos: DONE : Implement RoomPlacer with collision retry and seeded PRNG
DONE : Implement PrimMinimumSpanningTree with extra-edge probability pass
DONE : Write unit tests for determinism, non-overlap, empty-circle property, MST connectivity
changes-made: RoomPlacer: seeded Random, 1-unit buffer via 0.5 inflated-AABB intersect; validates size range and grid fit; maxAttempts caps the loop for infeasible configs

DelaunayTriangulation2D: Bowyer-Watson incremental insertion with super-triangle. In-circle test uses 3x3 determinant on doubles (floats lose precision near circumcircles when rooms sit on integer grids). CCW triangle ordering enforced by signed-area check. Output edges sorted (min,max) for byte-determinism

PrimMinimumSpanningTree: classic Prim's over Delaunay edges weighted by Euclidean distance between room centers, PriorityQueue ties broken by edge index for determinism. Extra-edge pass on separate RNG stream (seed XOR 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 golden-ratio constant) so extras reproduce independently of upstream RNG consumers. Default extraEdgeProb = 0.125 per vazgriz
Determinism verified by unit test: identical inputs -> byte-identical outputs across runs for all three algorithms

Unit tests: RoomPlacerTest (8), DelaunayTriangulation2DTest (7), PrimMinimumSpanningTreeTest (7). All 22 pass. Empty-circumcircle property verified across random 12-room placements. MST optimality verified on hand-constructed 5-room case with known-good weight=20
